html:
Malawi is a narrow, landlocked country in southeast Africa, running along the west shore of Lake Malawi. Britain ruled it as a protectorate, called Nyasaland from 1907, until independence in 1964.

From the 1500s the Maravi kingdoms ruled the area; the country's name comes from them. In the 1800s Ngoni raiders from the south and Yao slave traders working with the Swahili coast brought war. David Livingstone reached the lake in 1859, and Scottish missions followed. Britain declared a protectorate in 1891 to keep out the Portuguese.

  • 1915: John Chilembwe, a Baptist pastor, led a short rising against the treatment of Africans on settler estates.
  • 1953 to 1963: forced into the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, which most Africans opposed.
  • 1964: independence under Hastings Banda, who made himself president for life in 1971.
  • 1994: Banda lost the first multiparty election; power has changed hands peacefully since.
sum: Malawi is a narrow, landlocked country in southeast Africa, running along the west shore of Lake Malawi. Britain ruled it as a protectorate, called Nyasaland from 1907, until independence in 1964.
